The Contractor may include more than one species on the same PAR if those species are treated in the same location with the same pesticide (See Attachments – BMDO Pesticide Application Record (PAR)). As part of the PARs process, the Contractor shall provide onsite spot weather while applying the herbicide. Mixing Methods: All mixing shall be done to label, BLM, and state policies and requirements. This can include secondary containers, specific measurements and calibrations, spill containment and cleanup, and ensuring mix sites are in correct locations. The applicators and Contractor shall ensure they follow these policies. Quality Assurance and Quality Control Methods: The Contractor shall furnish equipment to monitor and ensure evenly spaced, straight, regular, and complete coverage of all areas included in the Contract. The Contractor shall ensure the correct spray rate is applied and that there is quality control in place to ensure the ground coverage is complete and accurate. Both the Contractor and the Government will conduct tests as operations progress to determine uniformity of application. The BLM COR/PI may utilize randomly placed drift cards. The Contractor shall provide to the Government: A written plan explaining how the Contractor will determine uniformity of

ntract. The contractor shall be responsible for purchasing, safely transporting, storing and disposal of the herbicide as follows: Herbicide *A BLM-approved Imazapic at 8 fluid ounces per acre. Adjuvants *BLM approved surfactant compatible with the application type, active ingredient, and applied at the rate identified on product’s labels. **See section 4.4 for the Chemical and Adjuvant options available for use within this contract. The contractor shall ensure the application of the herbicide meets all label specifications. The contractor shall be responsible for cleanup of accidental spills, following proper handling and storage precautions, and ensuring proper exposure control and personal protection is provided, as defined by the Herbicides’ and Adjuvants’ herbicide Safety Data Sheets. The contractor shall comply with all Federal, State, and Local regulations. Required Equipment Navigation: For ground applications, a GPS unit is required for tracking and data collection. The Contractor shall provide GPS tracks for any location where herbicide is applied. The system shall be sufficiently sensitive to provide an accuracy of ± 15ft in either the WGS84 or NAD83 datum. ponsible for giving the contractor any special instructions or guidance necessary to complete delivery as required by the contract. The COR and/or PI does not have the authority to modify or in any way amend the terms of this contract. Safety The Contractor is responsible for providing a safety plan that identifies a point of contact in the event of any accident. The plan should include names and emergency phone numbers for personnel and facilities to contact in case an emergency warrants such actions. The plan should also include a description of on-site emergency procedures to follow in case of an accident. The plan should identify the insurance company providing coverage and the pertinent group coverage number. In addition to being responsible for the safety of their employees, the contractor is also responsible for providing for the safety of the public during operations. This includes compliance with all OSHA and State of Nevada regulations for the use of equipment. Any hazards that would pose a danger to Contractor, Contractor’s personnel, the public or operating equipment should be identified, mitigated and/or avoided by the Contractor and brought to the Government representative’s attention.
